methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $299M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Electra, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Sandeep Nijhawan and Quoc Pham, is evaluated against a universe of 9 private and 1 public comparable (Linamar, LNZA). The peer set includes downstream Climate & Energy players at Series C stage: KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M).

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x multiplier to Electra's $299M total raised, implying $568M valuation. This method assumes standard venture step-up dynamics from Series B to subsequent rounds. The peer-median approach uses the three same-sector comparables, yielding a $1.0B median (range: $700M–$3.0B). This reflects actual valuations achieved by adjacent-stage companies in the same sector.

Synthesizing both methods produces a low-to-high range of $483M to $1.1B, with a median of $784M. The stage-progression result ($568M) sits in the lower half, reflecting Electra's earlier stage relative to the Series C peer set. The peer median at $1.0B assumes valuation parity with Electric Hydrogen and represents an upside case conditional on comparable execution and market timing. Key uncertainties center on the dispersion within the peer set—the $3.0B KoBold valuation significantly exceeds the median—and whether Electra's technology differentiation justifies premium positioning within this range.
